# R7 Digest — Pursuit 19–22 (11918–13416)
**Source:** Tsumura, *The First Book of Samuel* (NICOT, 2006)
**Reader:** extraction subagent R7
**Coverage:** raw lines 11918–13416 read in full (slice `R7_pursuit_19-22_11918-13416.txt`, slice-local L1–1500). Scope: **Saul’s Attempts to Kill David (19:1–21:1)** through **Saul’s Massacre of Nob’s Priests (22:6–23)**; early escapes (Nob, Gath, Adullam, Moab, Hereth).

## Claims

### C-R7-01 | Open death-order; Jonathan as mediator
- **Claim (Tsumura):** After indirect Philistine plots (18:17, 21, 25), Saul for the first time openly orders Jonathan and his officials to kill David (19:1). Jonathan’s loyalty as heir apparent is confirmed; he mediates between father and brother-in-law.
- **Quote:** “now (19:1) for the first time he openly announces his intention to his son Jonathan and his officials… Jonathan plays a crucial role as a mediator between Saul his father and David his brother-in-law”
- **Locus:** §E.1 intro / 19:1; pp. 489–490 / slice ~L1–13
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[saul]], [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R7-02 | Jonathan informs David; plan in the field (19:2–3)
- **Claim:** Jonathan warns David, plans to speak to Saul in the field, and report. Triple “my father” is ordinary address, not Klein’s “poignancy.” MT “sit… and hide” need not be inverted (McCarter); word-pair order may reverse. 20:19 refers back to this hiding. No need for McCarter’s “incomplete mixing of two versions.”
- **Quote:** “its use three times in vv. 2–3 has nothing to do with a ‘poignancy’ (Klein) in Jonathan’s speech.” / “No matter how close David was, it could not be certain that he would hear all the conversation.”
- **Locus:** 19:2–3; pp. 490–491 / ~L16–39
- **Targets:** [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-03 | Jonathan’s intercession: sin, innocent blood, bloodguilt (19:4–7)
- **Claim:** Jonathan addresses Saul formally as “king,” arguing David has not sinned; deeds “very good” = loyalty owed the king (McCarter: political nuances of love/loyalty/goodness). David “took his life in his hand” = risked life vs Philistine; Lord brought great victory. “Shedding innocent blood” (*bedām nāqî*) linked to Deut. and Manasseh; supreme for a ruler to avoid bloodguilt (foreshadows Abigail 25:30–31). Saul swears “As the Lord lives, he shall not be killed!”; David restored “as before.” Envelope structure “commit a sin… David.”
- **Quote:** “It is of supreme importance for the ruler to avoid bloodguilt.” / “here, it is Jonathan who plays the major role in interceding for and protecting David.”
- **Locus:** 19:4–7; pp. 491–492 / ~L42–86
- **Targets:** [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[saul]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-04 | Victory then second spear attack; “Lord’s spirit for evilness” (19:8–10)
- **Claim:** Philistine war; David’s great defeat may spur Saul’s anger. “Lord’s spirit for evilness” on Saul (as 16:14; 18:10); Tsumura sees no real difference from “God’s spirit for evilness” despite Block. Spear-pinning as 18:11. *pṭr “eluded”; “fled and escaped” (*nās wayyimmāleṭ*) key phrase; David fled and never returned.
- **Quote:** “Thus, David fled and never returned.” / “There does not seem to be any real difference in this phrase, used by the narrator also in 16:14, and ‘God’s spirit for evilness,’ used in 18:10”
- **Locus:** 19:8–10; pp. 492–493 / ~L88–112
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-05 | Escape theme until Gilboa; not McCarter’s 18:27 continuation
- **Claim:** Episode is sequel of v. 10’s “fled and escaped,” not McCarter’s broken continuation of 18:27. Narrative proceeds along David’s escapes until Saul dies on Mount Gilboa (ch. 31).
- **Quote:** “the narrative proceeds along the theme of David’s escapes from Saul until Saul himself dies on Mount Gilboa in ch. 31.”
- **Locus:** 19:11–24 intro; p. 493 / ~L114–117
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-06 | Michal’s ruse: window, teraphim, goats’ hair (19:11–13)
- **Claim:** Saul sends messengers to watch and kill David in the morning; Michal warns and lets him down through the window (// Rahab Josh. 2:15; Paul Acts 9:24–25). Not only Jonathan but daughter Michal intervenes. *Teraphim* (always plural form) here one human-size image (vs Laban’s small idols Gen. 31). *kebîr* “quilt” hapax; McCarter “tangle/net.”
- **Quote:** “Not only Saul’s son Jonathan but his daughter Michal intervenes as Saul tries to kill David.” / “The teraphim in the house of David and Michal was ‘of human size and shape.’”
- **Locus:** 19:11–13; pp. 493–494 / ~L119–139
- **Targets:** [[michal]], [[david]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-07 | Michal deceives messengers; “He is ill”; “Why should I kill you?” (19:14–17)
- **Claim:** Sending messengers in v. 14 is same incident as v. 11 (narrative backtrack; cf. 17:55)—focus shifts from Michal/escape to messengers/deception. Saul demands David brought in the bed to kill him; finds teraphim. Michal claims David threatened her life. Baldwin: children’s involvement intensifies love-hate.
- **Quote:** “We would rather take Saul’s sending messengers here as the same incident as that mentioned in v. 11.” / “‘the involvement of Saul’s children in the conflict between him and David intensifies the love-hate relationship.’”
- **Locus:** 19:14–17; pp. 494–495 / ~L141–171
- **Targets:** [[michal]], [[saul]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-08 | David to Samuel at Ramah/Naioth; “fled and came” series (19:18–19)
- **Claim:** David flees to Samuel at Ramah, informs him; they stay at Naioth. Visits to Samuel, Jonathan, Ahimelech precede wilderness. “Fled and came” marks serial unity (19:18 Samuel; 20:1 Jonathan; 21:11 Achish)—Grønbaek. Ramah ~2–3 miles north of Gibeah (&lt;1 hour); place of Saul’s first meeting with Samuel (ch. 9). Naioth (K. *nwyt*) related to *nāweh* “pasture/abode”; prophetic fraternities dwell in such settlements (// Mari *nawum*).
- **Quote:** “David visits and gets help from several people — Samuel, Jonathan, and Ahimelech — before taking to the wilderness.” / “each of the visits, which is introduced by and he came, constitutes a certain serial unity in the section as a whole (19:18–22:23).”
- **Locus:** 19:18–19; pp. 495–496 / ~L173–193
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[samuel]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-09 | Messengers prophesy; Samuel over “elders of the prophets”; spirit without techniques (19:20–21)
- **Claim:** Messengers see “elders of the prophets” (*lahăqat*) prophesying, Samuel “standing in charge.” Tsumura prefers *lhq* “elder” (Eth./Akk.) over *qhl* “company.” Spirit of God (*rûaḥ ’ĕlōhîm*) emphasized as 10:5; no ecstatic techniques noted—unexpected. Prophesying under God’s spirit has no inherent negative; Hitpael *hitnabbe’û* does not make it “ecstatic.” Prefer Parker’s “possession trance” vs “prophecy”; avoid “ecstasy” for non-Israelite phenomena. Wilson: ch. 10 controlled; 19:18–24 uncontrolled trance, Saul loses control—question complex. Threefold sending of messengers = epic pattern (// 2 K. 1; 1 Sam. 10:2–7).
- **Quote:** “no techniques used to get into an ecstatic state as in other extra-biblical religious practices are noted” / “the term ‘ecstasy’ is better avoided or used with restriction for the unusual and seemingly abnormal work of God’s spirit.”
- **Locus:** 19:20–21; pp. 496–498 / ~L195–220
- **Targets:** [[samuel]], [[saul]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R7-10 | Saul strips naked; second “Is Saul too among the prophets?”—negative reinterpretation (19:22–24)
- **Claim:** Saul goes via Secu’s “big cistern”; spirit comes; prophesies en route; strips garments; lies naked day and night before Samuel. “Naked” not necessarily total (Driver: inner tunic possible). Proverb “Is Saul too among the prophets?” given background a second time: in 10:11 surprise without contempt; here more negative—Saul abnormal under God’s spirit “for evilness.” Meaning of *mashal* determined by context. Mettinger: reversal of 10:1–9 endowment—spirit now makes Saul helpless, strips “clothes of a king.” R. P. Gordon/McKane: first occasion ecstatics unfit for Saul; now Saul unfit for them—“fraught with irony.” Chapter ends Saul negative/hopeless; David forced to escape again.
- **Quote:** “But this time the proverb is applied to Saul’s new situation and reinterpreted… The saying here has a more negative tone than it does in its original context.” / “In 19:18ff. it works in the reverse: it makes Saul helpless and drives him to strip off his clothes … the clothes of a king.”
- **Locus:** 19:22–24; pp. 498–500 / ~L221–257
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[samuel]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R7-11 | Last intimate Jonathan–David meeting; covenant rooted in Lord’s kindness (20 intro)
- **Claim:** Except Horesh (23:16–18), this is last reported meeting. Jonathan initiates covenant with David’s house (20:16); asks kindness when Lord cuts off David’s enemies (v. 15); confident David will rule (23:17). Swore for descendants/seed (v. 42). Love rooted in trust in Lord’s “goodness and mercy”; friendship “wonderful” (2 Sam. 1:26) only if seasoned by trust in One beyond them. David later favors Jonathan’s house (9:1).
- **Quote:** “Unless a friendship is seasoned by a taste of trust in the One who is beyond two of them, that friendship cannot be ‘wonderful’ (2 Sam. 1:26) as Jonathan’s friendship with David was.”
- **Locus:** §5 intro 20:1–24a; p. 500 / ~L259–261
- **Targets:** [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-12 | Chronology debate; Polzin continuity; David’s oath-like tricolon (20:1–4)
- **Claim:** Some place ch. 20 after spear (19:9–10) or window escape (McCarter 19:12) because Jonathan seems ignorant. Polzin: Jonathan’s naïve straightforwardness + David’s subterfuge + Saul’s obliviousness allow narrative cohesion—but does not solve chronology. “Fled and came” discourse transition. David’s triple “What…?” = poetic tricolon; may be oath-like (threefold as John 21); “still swore” (v. 3) continues that swearing. Double formula “as the Lord lives and your soul lives.” Jonathan: “Whatever you yourself say, I will do for you” (MT good sense vs McCarter/LXX).
- **Quote:** “the triple rhetorical questions in v. 1… could be like an oath” / “This indicates Jonathan’s naïvete of which David is well aware.”
- **Locus:** 20:1–4; pp. 500–504 / ~L263–347
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[jonathan]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-13 | New Moon plan; *ḥesed* and “covenant of the Lord” (20:5–11)
- **Claim:** New Moon (*ḥōdeš*) joyous festival; king as clan head; David as son-in-law expected. Day from sunset; “third evening” = evening of day after tomorrow; festival sometimes two nights if new moon unobservable. David’s cover story: yearly clan feast at Bethlehem. *ḥesed* = fidelity in covenant; *berît YHWH*—covenant in Lord’s name, witnessed by him (vv. 23, 42). Jonathan still naively supposes Saul would not harm David; field exit retards answer for suspense.
- **Quote:** “The covenant between Jonathan and David was a covenant of the Lord, in his name (v. 42) and witnessed by him (v. 23).” / “Jonathan is still naively supposes that his father Saul would not harm David”
- **Locus:** 20:5–11; pp. 504–506 / ~L349–427
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[jonathan]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-14 | Jonathan’s covenant with David’s house; *ḥesed YHWH*; “house of David” (20:12–17)
- **Claim:** Jonathan initiates sounding Saul; oath formula self-curse; “may the Lord be with you as he was with my father”—key phrase; past tense: Lord’s presence with Saul as past; clarifies inevitability of David’s succession (later Saul accepts 23:21). If Jonathan must die, he accepts; asks perpetual kindness for *my house* (= descendants; fulfilled Mephibosheth 2 Sam. 9). Jonathan’s house not among David’s enemies. “Made a covenant with the house of David”—brachylogy of *berît*; phrase later = Davidic dynasty (Tel Dan); here simply David’s descendants. “May the Lord hold David’s enemies responsible”—literal enemies (could include Saul), not euphemistic curse on David (against common view). Jonathan’s love personal more than political loyalty (vs Ashurbanipal vassal formula McCarter).
- **Quote:** “This gives ‘new clarity to the inevitability of David’s succession to the throne.’” / “Jonathan takes initiative in making a covenant with David’s house.” / “the past tense in as he was with my father … is important, for Jonathan takes the Lord’s presence with Saul as being in the past.”
- **Locus:** 20:12–17; pp. 506–510 / ~L429–556
- **Targets:** [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-15 | Stone Ezel; working day; arrow signal (20:18–24a)
- **Claim:** Wait three days; come after dark (*tērēd me’ōd* = sun goes down well, brachylogy of *šemeš*) on the **working day** (*beyôm hamma‘ăśeh*—day of business after festival, // Ezek. 46:1; Amos 8:5), not “when trouble began.” Temporal phrase modifies “come,” not “hid.” Stone Ezel may preserve Canaanite DN (// Ebenezer). Three arrows = several for practice cover (G. R. Driver). David hides in field.
- **Quote:** “the most natural meaning of the phrase beyôm hamma‘ăśeh (lit., ‘on the day of the work’) means ‘on the day of business,’ the day following the New Moon festival” / “what Jonathan suggests here is that David wait till it gets dark on the third day”
- **Locus:** 20:18–24a; pp. 510–515 / ~L557–624
- **Targets:** [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R7-16 | New Moon banquet; purity; “son of Jesse”; family feast (20:24b–29)
- **Claim:** Saul at wall seat; Jonathan stands in attendance (// Ugaritic Baal by El). First day Saul assumes ritual uncleanness (New Moon involves sacrifices). Second day: “son of Jesse” may show contempt (// 22:7–13; Doeg 22:9). Family feast (*zebaḥ mišpāḥāh*) yearly clan gathering—good excuse; Tsumura rejects Toorn/Malamat funerary-ancestor-cult reading (no real evidence; non-divine ancestors in Israel vs Canaanite deification). “My brother” (sg.) = Eliab; fratriarchy, Jesse retired—not father dead; MT preferred over LXX/4QSamᵇ plural.
- **Quote:** “it is unlikely that this gathering had the features of an ancestor cult of the Canaanite type.” / “The expression the son of Jesse, instead of ‘David,’ may be due to Saul’s reservation toward David, ‘perhaps from’ contempt.”
- **Locus:** 20:24b–29; pp. 515–519 / ~L626–699
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-17 | Saul’s rage at Jonathan; spear; hereditary kingship (20:30–34)
- **Claim:** Insult “son of a perverse, rebellious woman”; disgrace of mother’s nakedness = family shame. While son of Jesse lives, Jonathan’s kingship unestablished—vain appeal to self-interest; Jonathan already accepted (18:1–4; 20:14f.); hereditary monarchy taken for granted. *ben-māwet* = “he should be dead.” Saul casts spear at Jonathan; roles of David and Jonathan merge. Jonathan leaves in anger; pained for David (MT: final “him” = David; close identification).
- **Quote:** “this is ‘a vain appeal to Jonathan’s self-interest; for, although Saul spoke truly, Jonathan had already come to terms with the situation’” / “One might see here a merging of the roles of David and Jonathan.”
- **Locus:** 20:30–34; pp. 519–521 / ~L701–757
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-18 | Arrow signal enacted; farewell; eternal covenant of seed (20:35–21:1)
- **Claim:** Working-day morning; one arrow narrated but plural “arrows” gathered. Boy unknowing; secret message “beyond you” = danger. Meeting after signal strange but R. P. Gordon: strong emotions vs plans. David bows thrice; kiss/weep; David cries louder. “Go in peace!” = conclusio of successful negotiations (Wiseman), not mere farewell. Swore in Lord’s name = covenant before Lord (// 23:18 Horesh reconfirm). “Seed” replaces “house” (vv. 15–16); Jonathan again initiates eternal covenant. *hannegeb* “rock” uncertain (Mari *nagbu* stone/spring?).
- **Quote:** “Jonathan and David later reconfirm their covenant at Horesh (23:18).” / “Here again Jonathan takes initiative in making the ‘eternal covenant’ with David and his ‘seed.’”
- **Locus:** 20:35–21:1; pp. 521–524 / ~L759–826
- **Targets:** [[jonathan]], [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-19 | Excursus: two-day New Moon festival (ANE calendrical)
- **Claim:** ANE New Moon lasted one or two days depending on crescent visibility (Assyrian astrological texts; Ugaritic KTU 1.104). David knows “tomorrow” is new moon from waning moon before sunrise “today”; next visible new moon after sunset “day after tomorrow”—hence two-night festival at Saul’s court for household reintegration over sacrificial meal.
- **Quote:** “This is the reason why the New Moon festival was celebrated for two nights.” / “It was ‘an occasion for the reintegration of Saul’s household over a meal, probably of a sacrificial victim.’”
- **Locus:** Excursus after 20:42; pp. 525–526 / ~L829–975
- **Targets:** [[1-samuel]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R7-20 | Macrostructure 21:1–22:23: deception theme; narrative not scrap-heap
- **Claim:** Common theme deception: Nob and Gath. At Gath David unscathed (Ps 34); lies at Nob disastrous (22:18–19)—beginning of fugitive life. Structure: Nob (21:1–9) … Gath, Adullam, Moab, Judah (21:10–22:5) … Nob consequences (22:6–23)—not simple inclusio. Against McCarter’s “narrative scraps”: Gath understandable; Adullam between Gath and Saul’s hills, ~15 mi west of Bethlehem; Moab reasonable for parents (Ruth Moabite); Gad’s 22:5 forces return to Judah where he will be noticed—confidence Lord guides. Interrupted flow = mono-dimensional description of multi-dimensional reality.
- **Quote:** “Although at Gath David is able to get out, unscathed and thankful (see Psalm 34), his lies at Nob have disasterous consequences (1 Sam. 22:18–19).” / “the word of the prophet Gad… was almost a strong command to expose himself in a noticeable place, but he must have had confidence that the Lord would guide his life”
- **Locus:** §F intro + 21:1–22:5 intro; pp. 527–528 / ~L977–1042
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R7-21 | Nob: Ahimelech, holy bread, Doeg present (21:1–7)
- **Claim:** Nob ≈ el-‘Isāwîyeh N of Jerusalem, S of Gibeah—priestly city after Shiloh’s fall. Ahimelech son of Ahitub, brother of Ahijah (Saul’s chaplain), great-grandson of Eli, father of Abiathar; “the priest” = chief priest. Trembles (// Bethlehem elders 16:4). David’s cover story (secret royal mission) because unsure of trust (Ahijah’s brother)—deception leads to 22:6–23 disaster. Common vs holy bread; condition sexual abstinence (war purity; // Uriah 2 Sam. 11:11; Qumran War Scroll). *kelê* vessels likely euphemism for genitalia. Bread of Presence; five of twelve loaves; Sabbath observation evidence; Ahimelech bends rules (Jesus endorses mercy before ceremonial law, Matt 12 / Mark 2 / Luke 6). Parenthesis: Doeg the Edomite, chief leader of shepherds, “kept away before the Lord” (ceremonial detention); prepares 22:9–19. Edomites may enter Lord’s assembly (Deut. 23:7[8]).
- **Quote:** “Because Ahimelech was the brother of Saul’s chaplain Ahijah, David was probably not sure whether he could trust Ahimelech and hence made up a story… However, David’s deception resulted in the disaster in 22:6–23.” / “This verse prepares for the development of the present incident in 22:9–19.”
- **Locus:** 21:1–7; pp. 528–533 / ~L1044–1138
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]; **Misc (no established page):** Ahimelech, Doeg, Nob

### C-R7-22 | Goliath’s sword behind ephod; inexperienced liar (21:8–9)
- **Claim:** David requests weapon; Ahimelech gives Goliath’s sword wrapped in garment behind ephod—ephod here not garment but possibly image-type (// Gideon Judg. 8; Micah Judg. 17). David “There is nothing like it!”—fine sword, not merely available (vs Labuschagne). Contradicts earlier claim of urgency vs men’s purification time—David inexperienced liar; Ahimelech not used to deviousness.
- **Quote:** “David is obviously not an experienced liar. His statement that there was no time even to get a weapon contradicts his previous statement… but Ahimelech is not used to deviousness either and does not notice.”
- **Locus:** 21:8–9; pp. 533–534 / ~L1140–1170
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[philistines]], [[1-samuel]]; **Misc:** Ahimelech, Goliath’s sword / Nob

### C-R7-23 | Gath: Achish; feigned madness; “king of the land” (21:10–15)
- **Claim:** Real start of fugitive life (*arose and fled*). Geographic: Gath nearest Philistine city to Bethlehem beyond Elah; ~800 m down from hill country—leads toward ch. 27 settlement. Unprepared boldness alone with Goliath’s sword; common enemy Saul; may hope mercenary hire. Pss 34, 56 superscriptions. Achish name Philistine/Aegean (// Egyptian *kftiw*; Anchises; Ekron *’kyš* Ikausu). May be title/common name; Ps 34:1 “Abimelech” may be Semitic name for same. Servants: “king of the land” = local chieftain or different royal lexicon; Hertzberg: non-Israelites underline divine plan with David. Couplet 18:7 exact. Disguises judgment / feigns madness; spittle on beard. Madness superstition advantageous (R. P. Gordon). *mištaggēa‘* // prophetic ecstasy language elsewhere; Akk. *šegû* aggressive. Enter Achish’s house = become Philistine mercenary—refused now; later chs. 27, 29.
- **Quote:** “This is the real start of David’s life as a fugitive” / “One thing was clear: David and the Philistines now share a common enemy, Saul, king of Israel.” / “To enter Achish’s house means to become a mercenary for the Philistines. For now, David is chased away”
- **Locus:** 21:10–15; pp. 534–537 / ~L1172–1234
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[philistines]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-24 | Adullam: family; four hundred in straits (22:1–2)
- **Claim:** Cave of Adullam (not Wellhausen/McCarter “stronghold” emendation); Tell esh-Sheikh Madhkûr; ~10 mi ESE Gath, ~16 mi SW Jerusalem; midway Gath–Bethlehem; Judahite fortress Shephelah. Entire household in danger joins from Bethlehem. ~400: men in straits, with creditors, bitter spirit (*mar-nepeš*—Hannah, Ziklag, Danites, etc.). David chief of discontented/mistreated; passionate for change (// 2 Sam. 23:17).
- **Quote:** “Thus, David becomes the leader of everyone who had suffered some kind of loss or deprivation and were discontented, disenchanted, and mistreated in the society.”
- **Locus:** 22:1–2; pp. 538–539 / ~L1236–1248
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[1-samuel]]

### C-R7-25 | Moab: parents; “what God will do”; stronghold; Gad to Hereth (22:3–5)
- **Claim:** Mizpeh of Moab unknown; Ruth great-grandmother Moabite—parents safer; // Idrimi to mother’s kin. Moab Saul’s enemy (14:47)—willing to weaken him; later David defeats Moab (2 Sam. 8:2). “What God will do to/with me”—providential faith; “God” not Yahweh before non-Israelite. Stronghold ≠ Adullam cave (Gad: come to Judah); possibly Moab or Masada area; duration uncertain. Gad the prophet (later court prophet with Nathan; // Mari *muḫḫûm*) commands leave stronghold for Judah—likely via messengers; Forest of Hereth unknown (//? Horesh/Khirbet Khoreisa).
- **Quote:** “What God will do to/with me is in keeping with David’s faith in God who guides his life providentially, according to His will.” / “Gad, the prophet was, like Nathan, one of the ‘court prophets’ during David’s reign”
- **Locus:** 22:3–5; pp. 539–541 / ~L1250–1286
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[1-samuel]]; **Misc:** Gad the prophet, Mizpeh of Moab, Forest of Hereth

### C-R7-26 | Saul under tamarisk; Benjaminite rhetoric; Doeg’s report (22:6–10)
- **Claim:** Saul sits Gibeah under tamarisk with spear (// 18:10; 19:9; 20:33)—spear symbolizes kingship (// Assyrian bow/mace); “ruler under sacred tree” NW Semitic stock motif; burial under tamarisk Jabesh 31:13. Officers withhold info (David’s popularity). Rhetorical questions to Benjaminites: fields/vineyards, captains—consequences of kingship Samuel predicted (8:12, 14); feudal grants for warriors (Rainey; // Ziklag). Avoids name “David” (contempt). Conspiracy paranoia; “made a covenant” brachylogy *krt*; learned of 18:3/20:8 loyalty pact. Doeg “the Edomite” thrice (9, 18, 22)—foreigner betrays/kills. Doeg may lie re inquiring Lord (absent in 21:2–10) or escalate: inquire → provisions → Goliath’s sword as military aid narrative.
- **Quote:** “The spear symbolizes Saul’s ‘kingship’ or ‘kingly status’” / “it was a foreigner who betrayed David and killed the priests.” / “Not only does Doeg claim that Ahimelech inquired of God’s will for David, but he calls the holy bread ‘provisions,’ and refers to ‘the sword of Goliath’ — each statement more ‘military’ than the next”
- **Locus:** 22:6–10; pp. 541–543 / ~L1288–1361
- **Targets:** [[saul]], [[david]], [[jonathan]], [[1-samuel]]; **Misc:** Doeg, Ahimelech, Nob

### C-R7-27 | Massacre of Nob; runners refuse; Doeg kills 85; ḥerem on priestly city (22:11–19)
- **Claim:** All Ahimelech’s house summoned; clear conscience. Saul’s case: bread, sword, consulting God = conspiracy. Ahimelech: David incomparable trusted servant, son-in-law, bodyguard commander; not first consulting; family innocent (Mabee: judicial account; blameless David). Unjust judgment without proving David’s criminality—“How could an unjust judge be king over Israel?” (Mabee). Runners refuse to kill “priests of the Lord”—fear of Lord above king. Doeg kills 85 wearing linen ephod; foreigner/non-Yahwist? but was “detained before Lord”—perhaps formal liturgy without fear of God. Nob struck man/woman/child/infant/livestock “with edge of sword”—like ban (// 15:3) on priests’ city while Amalek spared; cruelty when reject God and justice. Central temple/national shrine; ark possibly at Nob. Key verb *sbb* “go around.”
- **Quote:** “Saul treated Nob like some enemy city that had been put under the ‘ban’ (cf. 15:3). Thus, Saul carried out ‘total destruction’ on the priests’ city, while neglecting to put the Amalekites under a ban in ch. 15.” / “When they reject God and his ‘justice,’ human beings can become cruel, totally destroying innocent people, and at the same time become tolerant toward the evil”
- **Locus:** 22:11–19; pp. 544–547 / ~L1363–1457

### C-R7-28 | Abiathar flees to David; Saul destroyer vs David preserver of priesthood (22:20–23)
- **Claim:** Abiathar (one/first son of Ahimelech) escapes and flees after David—word order reverse of David’s *mlṭ… brḥ*. **Focal contrast (Hertzberg):** Saul destroyer of priesthood; David its protector—gains “real” priest of Eli’s house; ephod comes with him (23:6); true priesthood, counsel, divine oracle move from Saul to David. Abiathar with David rest of fugitive life and reign (with Zadok); Solomon banishes him (1 K. 2:27) fulfilling Eli word (2:33 “only one man”). David accepts responsibility (*’ānōkî*; *sabbōtî* echoes *sbb* of massacre). “Stay with me… under protection.” Prepares ch. 23 oracles. Gordon: tragedy paves way for Jerusalem as chief sanctuary. Through tragedy God’s saving plan materializes. **Ongoing contrast:** Saul chases without priestly guidance; David “guided by the divine oracle at every turn.”
- **Quote:** “Thus, the narrative depicts Saul as the destroyer of the priesthood while David is its protector.” / “Thus, the true priesthood and priestly counsel and the divine oracle have officially moved from Saul to David.” / “It contrasts Saul as the destroyer of the priesthood of Nob with David as its preserver who saves ‘the cult of Yahweh from formal extinction in Israel.’ The following episodes continue to contrast Saul, who chases David without priestly guidance, with David, who is ‘guided by the divine oracle at every turn.’”
- **Locus:** 22:20–23; pp. 547–549 / ~L1459–1499
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[saul]], [[1-samuel]], [[samuel]] (Eli house trajectory); **Misc:** Abiathar, Ahimelech, Doeg, Nob
